newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-FINLAND RETAIN TEAM SKI JUMPING TITLE.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-FINLAND RETAIN TEAM SKI JUMPING TITLE.

text.p: Finland retained their ski jumping team title at the Nordic skiing world championships on Thursday with a provisional winning total of 955.3 points.
Finland, who won gold in 1995 in Thunder Bay, Canada, were second behind Japan after the first round.
But jumps beyond 120 metres by all four men in the second round allowed them to take first place while Japan ended second on 905 points.

Brilliant jumping by Dieter Thoma, who notched the day's best of 129.5 metres in his first effort before recording a 120 metres mark in the second round, lifted Olympic champions Germany to third place with 845.6 points.
The event started an hour late because of heavy snowfalls.
